adversely affect its business, prospects, financial condition, and results of operations.

risks.risk_name: Failure to compete successfully or excessive spending to remain competitive
risks.description: Cycurion may fail to compete successfully or be forced to spend heavily to keep up, risking adverse effects on its business and financial results.
risks.why: The company may need to expend significant resources to remain competitive, and if competitors are more successful in developing offerings or attracting customers, its business and financial results could be harmed.

metadata.source_text:
For all of these reasons, Cycurion may not be able
to compete successfully against its current or future competitors or may be required to expend significant resources in order to remain
competitive. If Cycurion’s competitors are more successful than Cycurion in developing new product and service offerings or in
attracting and retaining customers, Cycurion’s business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.

risks.risk_name: Products or professional services fail to detect vulnerabilities or identify and respond to cybersecurity incidents
risks.description: Failure of Cycurion's products or services to detect vulnerabilities or respond to cyberattacks may harm brand reputation and business results.
risks.why: If products fail to detect vulnerabilities or contain undetected errors, customers may delay or withhold payment, refuse to renew, or file liability claims, damaging reputation and operations (paragraphs 0, 1, 2).

metadata.source_text:
If our products or professional services fail
to detect vulnerabilities or identify and respond to cybersecurity incidents, or if our products contain undetected errors or defects,
our brand and reputation could be harmed, which could have an adverse effect on our business and results of operations.

risks.risk_name: Products falsely detect vulnerabilities or threats that do not exist
risks.description: Cycurion's products may generate false positives by detecting non-existent vulnerabilities or threats, undermining customer trust.
risks.why: The text explicitly states that products may falsely detect vulnerabilities or threats that do not actually exist, which can erode confidence in the solution (paragraph 1).

metadata.source_text:
If our products or professional services fail to
detect vulnerabilities in our customers’ cybersecurity infrastructure, or if our products or professional services fail to identify
and respond to new and increasingly complex methods of cyber-attacks, our business and reputation may suffer. There is no guarantee that
our products or professional services will detect all vulnerabilities, especially in light of the rapidly changing security landscape
to which we must respond. Additionally, our products may falsely detect vulnerabilities or threats that do not actually exist.

risks.risk_name: Products contain undetected errors or defects
risks.description: Undetected errors or defects in Cycurion's products may damage customer businesses and lead to liability claims or lost revenue.
risks.why: Errors, defects, or performance problems can damage customer businesses, cause significant costs, divert key personnel, and result in liability claims or non-renewals (paragraph 2).

metadata.source_text:
Our products may also contain undetected errors or
defects. Any errors, defects, disruptions in service, or other performance problems with our products may damage our customers’
businesses and could hurt our reputation. If our products or professional services fail to detect vulnerabilities for any reason, we
may incur significant costs, the attention of our key personnel could be diverted, our customers may delay or withhold payment to us
or elect not to renew or other significant customer relations problems may arise. We may also be subject to liability claims for damages
related to errors or defects in our products. A material liability claim or other occurrence that harms our reputation or decreases market
acceptance of our products may harm our business and operating results.

risks.risk_name: Association with customer data breaches harms market perception
risks.description: Even if not at fault, Cycurion may suffer reputational damage if a customer experiences a data breach due to mandatory public disclosures.
risks.why: Mandatory disclosures of customer data breaches often lead to negative publicity, and any association with such publicity may cause customers to lose confidence in Cycurion’s solutions (paragraph 3).

metadata.source_text:
Many federal, state, and foreign governments have
enacted laws requiring companies to notify individuals of data security breaches involving their personal data. These mandatory disclosures
regarding a security breach often lead to widespread negative publicity, and any association of us with such publicity may cause our
customers to lose confidence in the effectiveness of our security solutions. An actual or perceived security breach or theft of the sensitive
data of one of our customers, regardless of whether the breach is attributable to the failure of our products or professional services,
could adversely affect the market’s perception of our offerings and subject us to legal claims.

risks.risk_name: Failure to identify or consummate acquisitions limits growth
risks.description: Cycurion’s growth depends on successful acquisitions; failure to identify or complete them restricts expansion.
risks.why: The company states its growth strategy is driven by successful acquisitions, and growth is limited if it fails to identify and consummate acquisitions (paragraph 4).

metadata.source_text:
We
have recently acquired multiple businesses. Our growth strategy is driven by successful acquisitions and integration of additional businesses
that provide comparable or complementary services. Our ability to grow is limited if we fail to identify and consummate acquisitions.

risks.risk_name: Failed business collaborations or joint ventures reduce sales opportunities
risks.description: If potential joint ventures or collaborations fail to materialize, Cycurion may lose key sales and marketing opportunities.
risks.why: The company may lose sales and marketing opportunities if relationships fail to become significant agreements or if collaboration is inefficient (paragraph 5).

metadata.source_text:
We
have completed the acquisition of certain complementary businesses, and we intend to consider additional potential strategic transactions,
which could involve acquisitions of businesses or assets, joint ventures, or investments in businesses or technologies that expand, complement,
or otherwise relate to our business. We may also consider, from time to time, opportunities to engage in joint ventures or other business
collaborations with third parties. Should our relationships fail to materialize into significant agreements, or should we fail to work
efficiently with these companies, we may lose sales and marketing opportunities and our business, results of operations, and financial
condition could be adversely affected.

risks.risk_name: Risks from business acquisitions including integration challenges and resource diversion
risks.description: Acquisitions pose risks such as integration difficulties, resource strain, management distraction, and disruption of ongoing operations.
risks.why: Acquisitions require integration, strain systems and controls, divert management attention, and disrupt ongoing business (paragraph 6).

metadata.source_text:
Any
business acquisition creates risks such as, among others: (i) the need to integrate and manage the businesses acquired with our own business;
(ii) additional demands on our resources, systems, procedures, and controls; (iii) disruption of our ongoing business; and (iv)
diversion of management’s attention from other business concerns. Moreover, these transactions could involve: (a) substantial investment
of funds or financings by issuance of debt or equity securities; (b) substantial investment with respect to technology transfers and
operational integration; and (c) the acquisition or disposition of lines of businesses. Also, such activities could result in one-time
charges and expenses and have the potential to either dilute the interests of our existing stockholders or result in the issuance of,
or assumption of debt. Such acquisitions, investments, joint ventures, or other business collaborations may involve significant commitments
of financial and other resources. Any such activities may not be successful in generating revenue, income, or other returns, and any
resources we committed to such activities will not be available to us for other purposes. Moreover, if we are unable to access the capital
markets on acceptable terms or at all, we may not be able to consummate acquisitions, or may have to do so on the basis of a less than
optimal capital structure. Our inability to take advantage of growth opportunities or address risks associated with acquisitions or investments
in businesses may negatively affect our operating results.

risks.risk_name: Acquisitions require substantial capital and may dilute equity or increase debt
risks.description: Acquisitions may require significant funding through debt or equity issuance, risking dilution or unfavorable capital structure.
risks.why: Acquisitions may involve substantial investment via debt or equity issuance, potentially diluting existing stockholders or requiring debt assumption (paragraph 6).

risks.description: Acquisitions can incur one-time expenses and tie up resources without generating expected returns.
risks.why: Acquisitions may involve one-time charges, and committed resources may not generate revenue, income, or returns, making them unavailable for other uses (paragraph 6).

risks.risk_name: Inability to access capital markets hinders acquisition activity

risks.why: The company may not be able to consummate acquisitions or may have to do so on a less-than-optimal capital structure if it cannot access capital markets (paragraph 6).

risks.risk_name: Impairment of goodwill or intangible assets reduces earnings
risks.description: Impairment of assets from acquisitions or investments may materially reduce Cycurion’s reported earnings.
risks.why: Any impairment of goodwill or other intangible assets, or charges tied to acquisition/investment activity, may materially reduce earnings (paragraph 7).

metadata.source_text:
Additionally,
any impairment of goodwill or other intangible assets acquired in an acquisition or in an investment, or charges to earnings associated
with any acquisition or investment activity, may materially reduce our earnings. Future acquisitions or joint ventures may not result
in their anticipated benefits and we may not be able to properly integrate acquired technologies or businesses with our existing operations
or successfully combine personnel and cultures. Failure to do so could deprive us of the intended benefits of those acquisitions.

risks.risk_name: Failure to integrate acquired businesses or technologies reduces expected benefits
risks.description: Cycurion may fail to integrate acquired technologies or businesses, depriving it of anticipated benefits from acquisitions.
risks.why: Future acquisitions may not deliver anticipated benefits if Cycurion cannot properly integrate technologies, businesses, personnel, or cultures (paragraph 7).

metadata.source_text:
Additionally,
any impairment of goodwill or other intangible assets acquired in an acquisition or in an investment, or charges to earnings associated
with any acquisition or investment activity, may materially reduce our earnings. Future acquisitions or joint ventures may not result
in their anticipated benefits and we may not be able to properly integrate acquired technologies or businesses with our existing operations
or successfully combine personnel and cultures. Failure to do so could deprive us of the intended benefits of those acquisitions.

risks.risk_name: Failure to retain existing clients and attract new clients through acquisitions
risks.description: Failure to retain existing clients and attract new clients via acquisitions may prevent the company from achieving profitability.
risks.why: The company intends to grow its client base significantly through acquisitions, but if it fails to retain existing clients or attract new ones through these acquisitions, it may never achieve profitability (Paragraph 0).

metadata.source_text:
We
intend to grow our client base significantly through acquisitions of other service providers. If we fail to retain existing clients and
attract new clients through acquisitions, we may never achieve profitability.

risks.risk_name: Inability to grow sales in line with operational expansion
risks.description: If sales do not grow as operations expand, the company may continue to incur losses and remain unprofitable for an extended period.
risks.why: The company plans to expand operations and launch sales/marketing efforts, but if marketing efforts fail or sales do not grow accordingly, continuing losses may occur and profitability may be delayed (Paragraph 1).

metadata.source_text:
Through
acquisition of other service providers, we will inherit an increasingly larger client base, which creates cross-selling and up-selling
opportunities. We need high-quality service and exemplary client management to retain and grow our client base. We also plan to launch
sales and marketing efforts, and if our marketing efforts do not materialize, we may lose existing clients or fail to obtain new clients.
Our inability to grow sales as we expand in operations may result in continuing losses, and we may not be profitable for an extended
period of time. In addition, even if we are able to make future acquisitions, we will incur additional costs to consummate them, which
may result in a shortage in our capital resources. We may also incur difficulties in integrating new businesses with our current operations.

risks.risk_name: Capital shortage due to acquisition-related costs
risks.description: Costs associated with future acquisitions may deplete capital resources, creating a shortage.
risks.why: Even if future acquisitions are made, the company will incur additional costs to consummate them, which may result in a shortage of capital resources (Paragraph 1).

risks.risk_name: Difficulties in integrating acquired businesses
risks.description: Integrating newly acquired businesses with current operations may present operational challenges.
risks.why: The company may incur difficulties in integrating new businesses with its current operations after acquisitions (Paragraph 1).

risks.risk_name: Volatility in operating results due to client purchasing patterns and competition
risks.description: Revenue and operating results may fluctuate due to client purchasing patterns, competitive pricing, and increased client acquisition costs.
risks.why: Operating results depend on client purchasing patterns, competitive pricing, and debt servicing; revenue may fluctuate if sales targets are missed, new services are poorly received, or client acquisition costs rise due to competition (Paragraph 2).

metadata.source_text:
Our
operating results are dependent on a variety of factors, including purchasing patterns of our clients, competitive pricing, debt servicing,
and general economic trends. Our revenue and operating results may fluctuate if our sales targets are not met, new service offerings
receive poor client response, or client acquisition costs increase due to competition. In addition to these factors, our acquisition
strategy may impose additional risks to the predictability of our operating results. Revenue streams may be volatile due to the uncertainty
in identifying attractive acquisition candidates and our ability to consummate new acquisitions. Unexpected expenses may be incurred
during due diligence and post-acquisition. Management intends to manage risk carefully with the acquisitions; however, there can
be no assurance that we will be able to identity and consummate acquisitions that improve our results of operations.

risks.risk_name: Uncertainty in identifying and consummating attractive acquisitions
risks.description: Revenue streams may be volatile due to uncertainty in finding and completing suitable acquisitions.
risks.why: The acquisition strategy introduces risk to predictability of results because of uncertainty in identifying attractive acquisition candidates and the ability to consummate them (Paragraph 2).

risks.risk_name: Cyber-attacks targeting company systems or customer infrastructure
risks.description: Cyber-attacks may impair product performance, penetrate security, or misappropriate proprietary or customer information.
risks.why: As a cybersecurity provider, the company is a target of cyber-attacks designed to impede product performance, penetrate network security, or misappropriate proprietary or customer information (Paragraph 3).

metadata.source_text:
As a cybersecurity provider, we have been and will
likely be a target of cyber-attacks designed to impede the performance of our products, penetrate our network security, or that of our
customers, misappropriate proprietary information and/or cause interruptions to our services. If our systems are breached as a result
of third-party action, employee error or misconduct, attackers could learn critical information about how our products operate to help
protect our customers’ infrastructures from cyber risk, thereby making our customers more vulnerable to cyber-attacks. In addition,
if actual or perceived breaches of our network security occur, they could adversely affect the market perception of our products, negatively
affecting our reputation, and may expose us to the loss of our proprietary information or information belonging to our customers, investigations
or litigation and possible liability, including injunctive relief and monetary damages. Such security breaches could also divert the
efforts of our key personnel. In addition, such security breaches could impair our ability to operate our business and provide products
and services to our customers. If this happens, our reputation could be harmed, our revenue could decline and our business could suffer.

risks.risk_name: Reputational damage and loss of proprietary information from security breaches
risks.description: Actual or perceived security breaches could harm reputation, expose proprietary or customer data, and lead to litigation or liability.
risks.why: If breaches occur, they could adversely affect market perception, harm reputation, expose proprietary or customer information, and result in investigations, litigation, injunctive relief, or monetary damages (Paragraph 3).

risks.risk_name: Inadequate or unavailable insurance coverage for data security liabilities
risks.description: Insurance may not cover all data security liabilities, may be denied, or may become unavailable or unaffordable.
risks.why: Insurance may not be adequate for actual liabilities, may not cover indemnification claims, may be denied, or may not be available on reasonable terms or at all (Paragraph 4).

metadata.source_text:
Additionally, we cannot be certain that our insurance
coverage will be adequate for data security liabilities actually incurred, will cover any indemnification claims against us relating
to any incident, that insurance will continue to be available to us on economically reasonable terms, or at all, or that any insurer
will not deny coverage as to any future claim. The successful assertion of one or more large claims against us that exceed available
insurance coverage, or the occurrence of changes in our insurance policies, including premium increases or the imposition of large deductible
or co-insurance requirements, could have a material adverse effect on our business, including our financial condition, operating results,
and reputation.

risks.risk_name: Material adverse impact from uninsured or underinsured claims
risks.description: Large claims exceeding insurance coverage or changes in policy terms could materially harm financial condition and reputation.
risks.why: Successful assertion of large claims exceeding coverage, or policy changes like premium increases or higher deductibles, could materially adversely affect business, financial condition, and reputation (Paragraph 4).

risks.risk_name: Dependence on a few clients for a large portion of revenue
risks.description: A large portion of revenue comes from a few clients, creating vulnerability if any are lost.
risks.why: Currently, the company depends on a few clients for a large portion of revenue, and failure to meet their expectations could cause loss of these key clients (Paragraph 5).

metadata.source_text:
Currently, we are dependent on a few clients for
a large portion of our revenue. If we fail to provide professional services to these clients on a timely basis or fail to meet their
performance expectations, including the failure to enhance, maintain, upgrade, or improve our products and professional services, we
may lose some of our clients that generate a significant amount of our revenue. If this were to happen, we would need to acquire several
smaller clients or another large client to replace the lost revenue, as to which acquisitions there can be no assurance.

risks.risk_name: Inability to replace lost revenue from major clients through acquisitions
risks.description: Losing a major client may require acquiring multiple smaller or another large client to replace revenue, but such acquisitions are uncertain.
risks.why: If a major client is lost, the company would need to acquire several smaller clients or another large client to replace the revenue, but there is no assurance such acquisitions can be made (Paragraph 5).

risks.description: Loss of a significant customer increases per-client costs and reduces operating efficiencies.
risks.why: Any loss of a significant customer could increase per-client costs, decrease operating efficiencies, and materially adversely affect business, results, and financial condition (Paragraph 6).

all.

risks.description: The company cannot be certain it can mitigate the potential loss of any of its larger clients.
risks.why: There is no assurance that the company can easily mitigate, or even mitigate at all, the potential loss of any of its larger clients (Paragraph 6).

risks.risk_name: Delayed or reduced government spending due to budget impasses
risks.description: Failure of Congress or the Administration to approve appropriations or reach fiscal agreements could delay or reduce spending by government agencies we support.
risks.why: Failure to approve appropriations bills timely or reach fiscal agreements could delay and reduce spending by federal agencies and departments the company supports, causing loss of revenue, profit, and affecting cash flow (Paragraph 7).

metadata.source_text:
The failure of Congress to approve appropriations
bills in a timely manner for the Federal government agencies and departments we support, or the failure of the Administration and Congress
to reach an agreement on fiscal issues, could delay and reduce spending, cause us to lose revenue and profit, and affect our cash flow.

risks.risk_name: Delayed or cancelled funding due to congressional budget impasses or shutdowns
risks.description: Failure to pass appropriations bills or continuing resolutions can delay or cancel funding for Federal projects Cycurion supports, reducing revenue and profit.
risks.why: Congressional inability to agree on budgets leads to continuing resolutions or shutdowns, which delay or cancel payments for ongoing and new initiatives, directly impacting revenue and cash flow (para 0).

metadata.source_text:
On an annual basis, Congress is required to approve
appropriations bills that govern spending by each of the Federal government agencies and departments we support. When Congress is, or
Congress and the Administration are, unable to agree on budget priorities and, thus, unable to pass annual appropriations bills on a
timely basis, Congress typically enacts a continuing resolution. Continuing resolutions generally allow Federal government agencies and
departments to operate at spending levels based on the previous fiscal year. When agencies and departments operate on the basis of a
continuing resolution, funding we expect to receive from clients for work we are already performing and for new initiatives may be delayed
or cancelled. Congress and the Administration have from time to time failed to agree on a continuing resolution, resulting in temporary
shutdowns of non-essential Federal government functions and our work on such functions. Such shutdowns may result in delayed payments
to us and/or the delay of certain programs and projects for which we were engaged. Thus, the failure by Congress and the Administration
to enact appropriations bills in a timely manner can result in the loss of revenue and profit when Federal government agencies and departments
are required to cancel or change existing or new initiatives or the deferral of revenue and profit to later periods due to shutdowns
or delays in implementing existing or new initiatives. There is also the possibility that Congress will fail to raise the U.S. debt ceiling,
when necessary. This can also result in Federal government shutdowns. The delayed funding or shutdown of many parts of the Federal government,
including agencies, departments, programs, and projects we support, could have a substantial negative affect on our revenue, profits,
and cash flow.

risks.risk_name: Risk of non-payment or delayed payment from Federal government clients
risks.description: Federal clients may delay or fail to pay due to budget restrictions, shifting priorities, or disputes between Congress and the Administration.
risks.why: Government clients may restrict spending due to budgeting changes, OMB actions, or congressional disputes, leading to delayed payments or non-payment, forcing Cycurion to choose between damaging relationships or performing work at payment risk (para 1).

metadata.source_text:
We derived substantially all of our revenue in each
of 2024 and 2023 from contracts with Federal government clients. Selling to government entities can be highly competitive, expensive
and time consuming, and often requires significant upfront time and expense without any assurance that we will win a sale. Further expenditures
by our Federal government clients may be restricted or reduced by Administration or congressional actions, by action of the Office of
Management and Budget, by action of individual agencies or departments, or by other actions. Accordingly, we expect that, due to changing
government budgeting and spending priorities and related disputes among Congress and the Administration, some of our government clients
in the future may delay payments due to us, may eventually fail to pay what they owe us, and/or may delay certain programs and projects.
For some government clients, we may face a difficult choice: turn down (or stop) work due to budget uncertainty with the risk of damaging
a valuable client relationship or perform work with the risk of not being paid in a timely fashion or perhaps at all. Congressional elections
could also affect spending priorities and budgets at all levels of government. In addition, increased deficits and debt at all levels
of government, may lead to reduced spending by agencies and departments on projects or programs we support.

risks.risk_name: Challenges in selling cybersecurity solutions to government entities due to heightened sensitivity
risks.description: Government entities are highly cautious in purchasing cybersecurity products due to critical infrastructure and high visibility as cyber-attack targets.
risks.why: Government clients have heightened sensitivity around cybersecurity purchases because their IT infrastructures are critical, contain sensitive data, and are prime targets for cyber-attacks, making sales more difficult (para 2).

metadata.source_text:
Government entities also have heightened sensitivity
surrounding the purchase of cybersecurity solutions due to the critical importance of their IT infrastructures, the nature of the information
contained within those infrastructures and the fact that they are highly visible targets for cyber-attacks. Accordingly, increasing sales
of our products and professional services to government entities may be challenging.

risks.risk_name: Liability and reputational harm from mishandling sensitive government information
risks.description: Failure to safeguard sensitive government information accessed by employees or partners could lead to legal liability and reputational damage.
risks.why: Employees and channel partners may access sensitive government data, and any failure to maintain confidentiality could subject Cycurion to liability and reputational harm, adversely affecting operations (para 3).

metadata.source_text:
Further, in the course of providing our products
and professional services to government entities, our employees and those of our channel partners may be exposed to sensitive government
information. Any failure by us or our channel partners to safeguard and maintain the confidentiality of such information could subject
us to liability and reputational harm, which could materially and adversely affect our results of operations and financial performance.

risks.risk_name: Revenue and profit volatility from reliance on GSA Schedule and IDIQ contracts
risks.description: Revenue depends on competing for individual delivery/task orders under GSA and IDIQ contracts, leading to unpredictable income streams.
risks.why: These contracts require competing for each order, not guaranteeing ongoing work; significant costs are incurred bidding for orders that may be lost, and revenue is not assured at current levels (para 4 and 5).

metadata.source_text:
Our reliance on U.S. General Services Administration
Multiple Award Schedule (“GSA Schedule”) contracts and other Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (“IDIQ”)
contracts creates the risk of volatility in our revenue and profit levels.

risks.risk_name: Loss of business due to inability to compete under GSA Schedule or IDIQ contracts
risks.description: If government agencies use GSA or IDIQ contracts for services Cycurion cannot provide, it risks losing business and revenue.
risks.why: If agencies choose GSA/IDIQ contracts covering activities Cycurion cannot compete in or provide, it will lose business, directly negatively affecting revenue and profitability (para 5).

metadata.source_text:
We believe that one of the elements of our success
is our position as a prime contractor under GSA Schedule contracts and other IDIQ contracts, and we believe this position is important
to our ability to sell our services to Federal government clients. However, these contract vehicles require us to compete for each delivery
order and task order, rather than having a more predictable stream of activity during the term of a multi-year contract. In addition,
we may spend considerable cost and management time and effort to prepare bids and proposals for contracts, delivery orders, or task orders
that we may not win. There can be no assurance that we will continue to obtain revenue from such contracts at current levels, or in any
amount, in the future. To the extent that Federal government agencies and departments choose to employ GSA Schedule contracts and other
IDIQ contracts encompassing activities for which we are not able to compete or provide services, we could lose business, which would
negatively affect our revenue and profitability.

risks.risk_name: Acquisitions may be unsuccessful or exceed preferred price
risks.description: The company may face competitive acquisition markets where prices exceed preferred levels, or may fail to find suitable candidates, leading to unsuccessful acquisitions.
risks.why: The environment for acquisitions is very competitive and purchase prices will likely exceed what the company would prefer to pay; acquisitions completed may be unsuccessful.

metadata.source_text:
To remain competitive, we have in the past and may
in the future seek to acquire additional businesses, products, or technologies. The environment for acquisitions in our industry is very
competitive and acquisition candidate purchase prices will likely exceed what we would prefer to pay. We also may not find suitable acquisition
candidates, and acquisitions we complete may be unsuccessful.

risks.risk_name: Integration of acquisitions may be delayed or ineffective
risks.description: Integrating acquired operations, products, or technology may be complex, expensive, and time-consuming, potentially disrupting product development, sales, and operations.
risks.why: Integration is complex, expensive, and time-consuming, and may cause interruption or loss of momentum in product development, sales activities, and operations.

metadata.source_text:
Achieving the anticipated benefits of future acquisitions
will depend in part upon whether we can integrate acquired operations, products and technology in a timely and cost-effective manner
and successfully market and sell these as new product offerings, or as new features within our existing offerings. The acquisition and
integration processes are complex, expensive, and time consuming, and may cause an interruption of, or loss of momentum in, product development,
sales activities, and operations. If we are unable to effectively execute or integrate acquisitions, our business, financial condition,
and operating results could be adversely affected.

risks.risk_name: Limited due diligence may reveal unforeseen liabilities post-acquisition
risks.description: Due diligence on acquired companies may be limited, leading to discovery of inferior products or technology, and unforeseen liabilities exceeding negotiated warranty limits.
risks.why: Limited due diligence may reveal acquired products or technology were not as capable as thought, and unforeseen liabilities may exceed warranty and indemnity limitations.

metadata.source_text:
In addition, we may only be able to conduct limited
due diligence on an acquired company’s operations or may discover that the products or technology acquired were not as capable
as we thought based upon the initial or limited due diligence. Following an acquisition, we may be subject to unforeseen liabilities
arising from an acquired company’s past or present operations and these liabilities may be greater than the warranty and indemnity
limitations that we negotiate. Any unforeseen liability that is greater than these warranty and indemnity limitations could have a negative
impact on our financial condition.

risks.risk_name: Strategic partnerships may not be secured or yield commercial results
risks.description: The company may fail to secure additional strategic partnerships, or existing ones may not result in commercializable offerings or enhancements.
risks.why: No assurance can be given that additional partnerships will be secured, or that any relationship will continue, result in new offerings, or enhance existing ones.

metadata.source_text:
We and our subsidiaries have entered, and intend
to continue to enter, into strategic partnerships with third parties to support our future growth plans. We cannot provide any assurance
that we will be able to continue to enter into additional strategic partnerships. Strategic partnerships require significant coordination
between the parties involved, particularly if a partner requires that we integrate its products with our products. Further, we have invested
and will continue to invest significant time, money, and resources to establish and maintain relationships with our strategic partners,
but we have no assurance that any particular relationship will continue for any specific period of time, result in new offerings that
we can effectively commercialize, or result in enhancements to our existing offerings.

risks.risk_name: Loss of senior management or key employees could harm business objectives
risks.description: The departure of senior management or key employees, particularly Emmit McHenry, could significantly delay or prevent achievement of development and strategic objectives.
risks.why: Loss of services of senior management, particularly Emmit McHenry, or other key employees could significantly delay or prevent achievement of development and strategic objectives.

metadata.source_text:
Our future performance depends on the continued services
and contributions of our senior management, particularly Emmit McHenry, and other key employees to execute on our business plan and to
identify and pursue new opportunities and product innovations. From time to time, there may be changes in our senior management team
resulting from the termination or departure of our executive officers and key employees. The loss of the services of our senior management,
particularly Emmit McHenry, or other key employees for any reason could significantly delay or prevent the achievement of our development
and strategic objectives and harm our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

risks.risk_name: Third-party intellectual property infringement claims
risks.description: Accusations of intellectual property infringement by third parties, even if unfounded, could result in significant costs and harm business and operating results.
risks.why: Accusations of infringement, regardless of accuracy, could result in significant costs and harm business and operating results; claims may require royalty agreements or change business practices.

metadata.source_text:
Accusations against us by third parties of
infringement or other violations of their intellectual property rights, regardless of the accuracy of these assertions, could result
in significant costs and harm our business and operating results.

risks.risk_name: Infringement claims may prevent offering services or require unfavorable licensing
risks.description: Claims that services infringe third-party IP could harm reputation, require costly defense, and force changes to offerings or licensing on unfavorable terms.
risks.why: Claims could harm reputation, require significant expenses and monetary liability, prevent offering current services, or force entry into less-than-favorable royalty or licensing agreements.

metadata.source_text:
We cannot ensure that our professional services and
solutions, or the third-party solutions that we offer to our clients, do not infringe on the intellectual property rights of third parties
and, in the future, we may have infringement claims asserted against us or against our clients. These claims could harm our reputation,
require us to incur significant expenses and monetary liability, and prevent us from offering some of our current professional services
or solutions. Legal challenges to our intellectual property rights and claims of intellectual property infringement by third parties
could require that we enter into royalty or licensing agreements on less-than-favorable terms. Even if we believe any such challenges
or claims are without merit, they can be time-consuming and costly to defend, injure our reputation, and divert management’s attention
and resources away from our business. We may need to change our business practices if any of these events were to occur, which may limit
our ability to compete effectively and could have an adverse effect on our results of operations.

risks.risk_name: Third-party software license changes may disrupt operations
risks.description: Increases in third-party software license fees or changes to terms may require vendor or system changes, impacting services and operational processes.
risks.why: License fees could increase, or terms may change, requiring changes to vendors or IT systems, which could impact solutions provided to clients or operational support processes.

metadata.source_text:
Significant portions of our services and operations
rely on software that is licensed from third-party vendors. The fees associated with these license agreements could increase in future
periods, resulting in increased operating expenses. If there are significant changes to the terms and conditions of our license agreements,
or if we are unable to renew these license agreements, we may be required to make changes to our vendors or information technology systems.
These changes could impact the solutions and services we provide to our clients or the processes we have in place to support our operations,
which could have an adverse effect on our business.

risks.risk_name: Material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting
risks.description: Material weaknesses in internal controls could impair reliable financial reporting and business decision-making.
risks.why: Management must assess and disclose material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting under SOX Section 404, and such weaknesses could harm business, investor confidence, stock price, and access to financing.

metadata.source_text:
In the future, under Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley
Act of 2002 (the “SOX Act”), we will be required to furnish a report by our management on internal control over financial
reporting. This report must contain, among other matters, an assessment of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting,
including a statement as to whether or not our internal control over financial reporting is effective. This assessment must include disclosure
of any material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting identified by our management.

risks.risk_name: Material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting
risks.description: Failure to maintain effective internal controls could lead to regulatory investigations or sanctions.
risks.why: Ineffective internal control over financial reporting could result in investigations or sanctions by regulatory authorities, as stated in paragraph [1].

metadata.source_text:
We identify material weakness in our internal controls, which could affect
our ability to provide reliable financial statements and our business decision-making process, could harm our business and operating results,
cause investors to lose confidence in our reported financial information, cause the market price of our securities to decrease and harm
our ability to obtain additional financing, especially additional financing on favorable terms, could be adversely affected. In addition,
failure to maintain effective internal control over financial reporting could result in investigations or sanctions by regulatory authorities.
For a description of our material weaknesses, please see “Item 9A. Controls and Procedures.”

risks.risk_name: Strain on operations and resources from rapid growth
risks.description: Significant expansion of operational activities may strain business operations, finances, and management resources.
risks.why: The company intends to expand operations significantly, which could place a strain on operations, finances, management, and other resources, as listed in paragraph [2].

metadata.source_text:
In the near term, we intend to expand the scope of
our operational activities significantly. If we are successful in executing our business plan, we will experience growth in our business
that could place a significant strain on our business operations, finances, management, and other resources. The factors that may place
strain on our resources include, but are not limited to, the following:

risks.risk_name: Inability to manage rapid growth effectively
risks.description: Rapid growth may overwhelm administrative and operational resources, hindering effective management.
risks.why: Rapid growth requires substantial expansion of administrative and operational capabilities and successful recruitment/retention of qualified personnel, which cannot be assured per paragraph [3].

metadata.source_text:
Additionally, our strategy envisions a period of
rapid growth that may impose a significant burden on our administrative and operational resources. Our ability to manage growth effectively
will require us to expand the capabilities of our administrative and operational resources substantially and to attract, train, manage,
and retain qualified management and other personnel. There can be no assurance that we will be successful in recruiting and retaining
new employees or retaining existing employees.

risks.risk_name: Failure to manage growth successfully
risks.description: Inability to manage growth may result in sales not increasing commensurately with capital investments.
risks.why: Failure to manage growth could cause sales to not increase with capital investments or materially adversely affect business, financial condition, or results of operations, as stated in paragraph [5].

metadata.source_text:
We cannot provide assurances that our management
will be able to manage this growth effectively. Our failure to manage growth successfully could result in our sales not increasing commensurately
with capital investments, if at all, or otherwise materially adversely affecting our business, financial condition, or results of operations.

risks.risk_name: Dilution of ownership through future equity issuances
risks.description: Issuance of additional shares without shareholder approval may dilute ownership and depress share price.
risks.why: The company may issue additional shares of common stock or other equity securities without stockholder approval, which would dilute ownership interests and may depress market price, per paragraph [5].

metadata.source_text:
We may issue additional shares of Cycurion
common stock or other equity securities without your approval, which would dilute your ownership interests and may depress the market
price of your shares.

risks.risk_name: Dilution of ownership through future equity issuances
risks.description: Future equity issuances for acquisitions, debt repayment, or incentive plans may occur without shareholder approval.
risks.why: Additional shares may be issued without stockholder approval in connection with acquisitions, repayment of indebtedness, or under the Equity Incentive Plan, as specified in paragraph [6].

metadata.source_text:
We may issue additional shares of Cycurion common
stock or other equity securities of equal or senior rank in the future in connection with, among other things, future acquisitions, repayment
of outstanding indebtedness or under the Equity Incentive Plan, without stockholder approval, in a number of circumstances.

risks.risk_name: Failure to develop market-accepted innovations
risks.description: Inability to develop or market new solutions and sales policies may fail to meet customer needs or generate returns.
risks.why: Success depends on personnel's creative and marketing skills and ability to appeal to customers and manufacturers; failure could adversely affect business, financial condition, or results of operations per paragraph [7].

metadata.source_text:
In the area of innovation, we must be able to add
new solutions and professional service offerings and adopt sales incentives and policies that appeal to our customers and prospective
customers. This depends, in part, on the creative and marketing skills of our personnel and on our ability to appeal to both customers
and manufacturers. We may not be successful in the development, introduction, marketing and sourcing of new products or sales policies
that satisfy customer needs, achieve market acceptance, or generate satisfactory financial returns, any of which could adversely affect
our business, financial condition, or results of operations.

risks.risk_name: Counterparties may not approve assignment of SLG agreements
risks.description: Counterparties to SLG agreements may refuse to assign contracts to Cycurion, preventing it from becoming prime contractor.
risks.why: There is no guarantee counterparties will approve assignment to Cycurion, which would result in Cycurion becoming prime contractor, as stated in paragraph [8] and [9].

metadata.source_text:
There is no guarantee that our possible assumption
of any or all of the to-be-assigned SLG agreements, which, if assumed by us, would result in our becoming the prime contractor thereunder,
will be approved by the counterparties. Mitigating factors that may hinder its acquisition include:

risks.risk_name: Incomplete due diligence on SLG agreements
risks.description: Due diligence may fail to reveal all relevant information about SLG agreements, risking unforeseen costs or failed assumptions.
risks.why: The company relies on information from SLG and its advisors, with no assurance of receiving all relevant data or identifying factors that could prevent assumption or cause financial costs, per paragraph [10].

metadata.source_text:
●
The
                                            counterparty to one or more of the to-be-assigned SLG agreements, which, if assumed by us,
                                            would result in our becoming the prime contractor thereunder, does not approve the relevant
                                            assignment to us.

risks.risk_name: Unforeseen costs related to assumption of SLG agreements
risks.description: Cycurion may incur significant unforeseen costs if it assumes the SLG agreements and becomes prime contractor, including legal, due diligence, integration, and consolidation expenses.
risks.why: Paragraphs [0] and [1] state that assuming the SLG agreements would make Cycurion prime contractor and could result in significant unforeseen costs, including legal, due diligence, integration, and consolidation costs not present as a subcontractor.

metadata.source_text:
We may incur significant unforeseen costs related
to our possible assumption of the to-be-assigned SLG agreements, which, if assumed by us, would result in our becoming the prime contractor
thereunder, that are the subject of the SLG Assignment Agreement.

risks.risk_name: Increased interest expense and leverage from debt
risks.description: Cycurion may increase its interest expense, leverage, and debt service requirements if it incurs additional debt to fulfill obligations under the assumed SLG agreements.
risks.why: Paragraph [2] explicitly states that incurring additional debt to meet obligations under the to-be-assigned SLG agreements (which would make Cycurion prime contractor) could increase interest expense, leverage, and debt service.

metadata.source_text:
●
Increase
                                            our interest expense, leverage, and debt service requirements if we incur additional debt
                                            to in connection with the obligations that we will assume under the to-be-assigned SLG agreements,
                                            which, if assumed by us, would result in our becoming the prime contractor thereunder;

risks.risk_name: Inability to integrate as prime contractor
risks.description: Cycurion may fail to integrate the SLG agreements into its business model as prime contractor, causing significant disruption.
risks.why: Paragraphs [3] and [4] state there is no assurance Cycurion can integrate becoming prime contractor into its current subcontractor model, which could disrupt business and impede realization of benefits.

metadata.source_text:
There is no assurance that we will be able
to integrate becoming the prime contractor under the to-be-assigned SLG agreements into our business model, which could then result in
significant disruption to our business.

risks.risk_name: Counterparties may not approve assignment of SLG agreements
risks.description: Counterparties to the SLG agreements may refuse to approve Cycurion’s assumption of the contracts, preventing it from becoming prime contractor.
risks.why: Paragraphs [5] and [6] state there is no assurance counterparties will permit assignment, as each agreement requires their approval, even though Cycurion is already known as the prime subcontractor.

metadata.source_text:
There is no assurance that any or all the counterparties
to the to-be-assigned SLG agreements, which, if we are able to assume, would result in our becoming the prime contractor thereunder,
will permit such assignment by SLG and assumption by us.

risks.risk_name: SLG agreements may not perform at current levels post-assumption
risks.description: The to-be-assigned SLG agreements may not operate at current or historic levels after Cycurion becomes prime contractor, increasing costs.
risks.why: Paragraph [7] states there is no assurance the agreements will continue at current levels, and as prime contractor, Cycurion’s costs would be higher than as subcontractor.

metadata.source_text:
There is no assurance that the to-be-assigned SLG
agreements, which, if assumed by us, would result in our becoming the prime contractor thereunder, will continue to operate at current
or historic levels. Although we have no reason to believe otherwise, that is the same risk that we face as the prime subcontractor for
such agreements; however, as the prime contractor under such agreements, our costs would be higher than they currently are.

risks.risk_name: Inadequate insurance coverage
risks.description: Cycurion may not have adequate insurance coverage for business risks, exposing it to substantial uninsured liabilities.
risks.why: Paragraph [8] states Cycurion carries insurance for most risks but may not have adequate coverage, and any significant uninsured liability could adversely affect cash position and operations.

metadata.source_text:
We carry insurance for most categories of risk that
our business may encounter; however, we may not have adequate levels of coverage. We currently maintain general liability, property,
workers’ compensation, clinical study, products liability and directors’ and officers’ insurance, along with an umbrella
policy. We may not be able to maintain existing insurance at current or adequate levels of coverage. Any significant uninsured liability
may require us to pay substantial amounts, which would adversely affect our cash position and results of operations.

risks.risk_name: Failure to maintain effective internal control over financial reporting
risks.description: Failure to maintain proper internal controls could impair Cycurion’s ability to produce accurate financial statements, harming investor confidence and stock value.
risks.why: Paragraph [10] states that failure to maintain effective internal controls could impair accurate and timely financial reporting, harming results, investor views, and stock value.

metadata.source_text:
If we fail to maintain proper and effective
internal control over financial reporting in the future, our ability to produce accurate and timely financial statements could be impaired,
which could harm our operating results, investors’ views of us, and, as a result, the value of our common stock.

risks.risk_name: Inability to comply with Sarbanes-Oxley Section 404 requirements
risks.description: Cycurion may fail to meet Sarbanes-Oxley Section 404 requirements for internal control reporting, leading to loss of investor confidence and stock price decline.
risks.why: Paragraph [11] states that if management or auditors cannot conclude internal controls are effective, investors may lose confidence and the stock price may decline, due to complex compliance requirements.

metadata.source_text:
Pursuant to Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act,
our management will be required to report upon the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting beginning with the
annual report for our fiscal year ending December 31, 2024. When and if we are a “large accelerated filer” or an “accelerated
filer” and are no longer an “emerging growth company” or “smaller reporting company,” each as defined in
the Exchange Act, our independent registered public accounting firm will be required to attest to the effectiveness of our internal control
over financial reporting. However, for so long as we remain an emerging growth company or smaller reporting company, we intend to take
advantage of an exemption available to emerging growth companies and smaller reporting companies from these auditor attestation requirements.
The rules governing the standards that must be met for management to assess our internal control over financial reporting are complex
and require significant documentation, testing, and possible remediation. To comply with the requirements of being a reporting company
under the Exchange Act, we will need to upgrade our systems including information technology; implement additional financial and management
controls, reporting systems, and procedures; and hire additional accounting and finance staff. If we or, if required, our auditors are
unable to conclude that our internal control over financial reporting is effective, investors may lose confidence in our financial reporting,
and the trading price of our common stock may decline.

risks.risk_name: Investors may find our common stock less attractive because we may rely on emerging growth company exemptions
risks.description: Relying on emerging growth company exemptions may reduce disclosure and make Cycurion's stock less attractive to investors.
risks.why: The company may use exemptions like reduced financial disclosures, no auditor attestation under Section 404(b), and less executive compensation detail, which could cause investors to view its stock less favorably, potentially leading to a less active trading market and higher volatility (Paragraphs 0, 1, 2).

metadata.source_text:
We are an emerging growth company and are eligible
to take advantage of certain exemptions from various reporting requirements that are applicable to other public companies that are not
emerging growth companies, including, but not limited to, only two years of audited financial statements in addition to any required
unaudited interim financial statements with correspondingly reduced “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition
and Results of Operations” disclosure, not being required to comply with the auditor attestation requirements of Section 404 of
the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 reduced disclosure obligations regarding executive compensation in this Annual Report and our periodic
reports and proxy statements, exemptions from the requirements of holding non-binding advisory votes on executive compensation and seeking
stockholder approval of any golden parachute payments not previously approved and not being required to adopt certain accounting standards
until those standards would otherwise apply to private companies. We could be an emerging growth company until the last day of the fiscal
year following the fifth anniversary of this offering, although circumstances could cause us to lose that status earlier, including if
we become a large accelerated filer (in which case we will cease to be an emerging company as of the date we become a large accelerated
filer, which, generally, would occur if, at the end of a fiscal year, among other things, the market value of our common stock that is
held by non-affiliates exceeds $700 million as of the last business day of our most recently completed second fiscal quarter), if we
have total annual gross revenue of $1.235 billion or more during any fiscal year (in which cases we would no longer be an emerging growth
company as of March 31 of such fiscal year), or if we issue more than $1.0 billion in non-convertible debt during any three year period
before that time (in which case we would cease to be an emerging growth company immediately). Even after we no longer qualify as an emerging
growth company, we may still qualify as a “smaller reporting company,” which would allow us to take advantage of many of
the same exemptions from disclosure requirements including not being required to comply with the auditor attestation requirements of
Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and reduced disclosure obligations regarding executive compensation in this Annual Report and our
periodic reports and proxy statements. We cannot predict if investors will find our common stock less attractive because we may rely
on these exemptions. If some investors find our common stock less attractive as a result, there may be a less active trading market for
our common stock and our stock price may be more volatile.

risks.risk_name: Reduced auditor attestation under Section 404(b) of Sarbanes-Oxley Act
risks.description: Cycurion is not required to comply with auditor attestation on internal controls over financial reporting as an emerging growth company.
risks.why: As an emerging growth company, Cycurion is exempt from Section 404(b) auditor attestation requirements, which may reduce investor confidence in financial reporting reliability (Paragraphs 0, 2).

risks.risk_name: Exemption from say-on-pay and golden parachute advisory votes
risks.description: Cycurion is not required to hold non-binding advisory votes on executive compensation or golden parachute payments.
risks.why: As an emerging growth company, Cycurion is exempt from say-on-pay, say-on-frequency, and say-on-golden-parachute voting requirements under the JOBS Act, reducing shareholder oversight (Paragraph 2).

metadata.source_text:
Cycurion will qualify as an “emerging growth
company” as defined in Section 2(a)(19) of the Securities Act, as modified by the JOBS Act. As such, Cycurion will be eligible
for and intends to take advantage of certain exemptions from various reporting requirements applicable to other public companies that
are not emerging growth companies for as long as it continues to be an emerging growth company, including (a) the exemption from the
auditor attestation requirements with respect to internal control over financial reporting under Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley
Act, (b) the exemptions from say-on-pay, say-on-frequency, and say-on-golden parachute voting requirements, and (c) reduced disclosure
obligations regarding executive compensation in its periodic reports and proxy statements. Cycurion will remain an emerging growth company
until the earliest of (i) the last day of the fiscal year in which the market value of common stock that is held by non-affiliates exceeds
$700 million as of June 30 of that fiscal year, (ii) the last day of the fiscal year in which it has total annual gross revenue of $1.235
billion or more during such fiscal year (as indexed for inflation), (iii) the date on which it has issued more than $1 billion in non-convertible
debt in the prior three-year period, or (iv) the last day of the fiscal year following the fifth anniversary of the date of the first
sale of its predecessor’s IPO. In addition, Section 107 of the JOBS Act also provides that an emerging growth company can take
advantage of the exemption from complying with new or revised accounting standards provided in Section 7(a)(2)(B) of the Securities Act
as long as Cycurion is an emerging growth company. An emerging growth company can therefore delay the adoption of certain accounting
standards until those standards would otherwise apply to private companies. We have elected not to opt out of such extended transition
period and, therefore, Cycurion may not be subject to the same new or revised accounting standards as other public companies that are
not emerging growth companies. Investors may find our common stock less attractive because Cycurion will rely on these exemptions, which
may result in a less active trading market for our common stock and its price may be more volatile.

risks.risk_name: Delayed adoption of new or revised accounting standards
risks.description: Cycurion can delay adopting new accounting standards until they apply to private companies.
risks.why: Under Section 107 of the JOBS Act, Cycurion elected not to opt out of the extended transition period, so it may not adopt new accounting standards at the same time as other public companies (Paragraph 2).
